## My request:
시각 의미 데이터와 후보 데이터에 반영해줘. 그 다음 스킬의 최신 버전을 사용하여 독립된 서브에이전트 3개에서 각각 서로 다른 컨셉으로 이번에 반영한 주제가 이미지에 실제로 반영되는지까지 테스트할 수 있는 랜덤한 복잡한 컨셉을 정하여 테스트케이스를 마련하고 첨부한 이미지를 활용하여 프롬프트 작성하고 이미지 생성하도록 하여 잘 반영되었는지 테스트해줘.
interpreted_intent: The requester asks for three independent complex random photographic generation tests of the preceding winter-fashion integration, using the supplied image. This arm independently interprets that topic through knit structure and garment layering. The selected seed picks a winter orchard caretaker labeling a branch at the shed threshold. A small purposeful act, the damp trace of brought-in snow and connected wearable layers make the scene readable in one image. The intimate but ordinary concentration and soft doorway light supply subtle supporting sensual appeal at the saved level 1; fetish and surreal add no treatment. All wardrobe, pose, place, age presentation, scene history and camera choices are agent-owned and remain open. General-knowledge alternatives included tram, seed-swap, kiln, observatory, ferry and orchard settings; the uniform seeded draw chose the orchard. The familiar working scene is chosen for a clear hierarchy rather than spectacle.
subject: A woman whose visible face and short dark bob are guided by the supplied image; human primary subject.
setting: The threshold of a timber potting shed in a snow-covered orchard, with a waist-high wooden workbench.
event: Wearing winter clothing while attaching a paper label to a branch resting on the workbench.
visual_priorities: Raised cable ridges and recessed stitch channels identify the oatmeal cardigan surface, while narrow parallel ribs finish its edges.
Pine-green geometric colorwork belongs to the separate knitted vest under the open cardigan; the white collar, cuffs and hem connect to the innermost shirt.
The charcoal rib-knit scarf lies behind the neck and down the outer sides, leaving the exposed vest chest readable.
A twig resting on the bench, left-hand stabilization, right-hand string ends and hanging label connect the labeling task in one readable moment.
Warm shed light on her softly concentrated face contrasts with snowy orchard light, giving tactile clothing and quiet presence a shared hierarchy.
baseline_prompt_en: This winter clothing photograph shows a woman whose face and hair are guided by the supplied image, wearing winter clothing in connected layers. Her short dark bob has fine wispy bangs, brown eyes, softly rounded cheeks and natural rose lips. At the threshold of a timber potting shed in a snow-covered orchard, she has just brought a bare apple branch inside and is attaching a small paper label before returning it to a propagation box. The branch rests horizontally on a waist-high wooden workbench below her chest, its snowy twig tips extending toward the open doorway. Her left fingertips press the branch gently against the bench, while her right thumb and index finger pinch the ends of a loose cotton string already looped around the branch and through the label hole; the label hangs below the branch. Her elbows stay bent near her own torso, her wrists hover above the worktop, and her feet support her relaxed upright stance behind the bench. Her concentrated eyes follow the knot; her slightly parted lips and softened cheek in the warm doorway light give the moment a quietly attractive, approachable presence. She wears an oatmeal wool cable-knit cardigan with its front open. Raised interlacing cable columns curve over and under one another across the cardigan body and sleeves, separated by recessed stitch channels; individual knit loops and soft wool fibers catch the light on the ridge crests. Separate narrow parallel rib-knit columns finish the cardigan cuffs, lower hem and open front edges. Beneath the cardigan is a pine-green sleeveless Fair Isle wool vest: small cream and rust geometric colorwork stitches repeat in horizontal bands across its exposed chest, with each motif sharing the continuous knitted ground rather than floating above it. A white cotton shirt is the innermost layer, its pointed collar rising above the vest neckline, a narrow shirt cuff emerging below each cardigan cuff, and a thin straight shirt hem showing below the vest and open cardigan. The collar, cuffs and hem belong to that same underlayer, with the cardigan outside the vest and the vest outside the shirt. A long charcoal rib-knit scarf passes behind her neck; its two ends descend along the outer sides of the open cardigan, leaving the center chest and vest motifs visible. Long parallel raised ribs and recessed channels run down the scarf, distinct from the crossing cable relief of the cardigan. Dark wool trousers extend beneath the shirt hem. The open shed door frames blue snow and orderly rows of bare orchard trees behind her, while a small propagation box with other labeled twigs sits at one side of the workbench. Snow crystals cling to the branch ends, and a damp mark beneath them links the recent outdoor cold to the current indoor task. A vertical three-quarter photograph runs from the crown of her head to mid-thigh, showing both hands and the full exposed cardigan front, vest chest, scarf ends and layered hems. The camera sees her from a gentle front three-quarter position at chest height, close enough to resolve the knit structures; a natural 50mm perspective keeps her body and tabletop connected. Cool daylight from the open doorway and warm side light inside the shed separate pale wool relief, flat geometric stitch colors and crisp cotton edges. Her face, hands and central garment layers are sharply readable, with softer orchard detail behind. The scene feels inhabited and observant, its winter fashion understood through the differing tactile surfaces and the small useful action happening within them.
